speaker: Customer

options.text: I understand. Price is important. Can I ask what you’re comparing us to?

why: You validate the concern, then gather comparison context before defending price.
psychology: People lower resistance when they feel heard before being persuaded.
application: In pricing objections, ask for the alternative they are weighing.

speaker: Customer
prompt: I’ve been on hold for twenty minutes!

options.text: I’m sorry for the wait. Thank you for staying—how can I help right now?

why: Apology plus gratitude plus forward action rebuilds trust fast.
psychology: Acknowledgment reduces anger; a clear next step restores control.
application: Lead with empathy, then move straight into problem-solving.

speaker: Customer

options.text: Are you sure you ordered the right thing?
That’s frustrating. Let’s fix it—can you confirm the order number?

why: You own the emotion and request only the data needed to resolve it.
psychology: Blame triggers defensiveness; ownership invites cooperation.
application: Name the frustration, then ask one precise clarifying question.

speaker: Customer
prompt: I want a full refund immediately.

options.text: I can help. Let me review your case and explain the fastest options.

why: You stay helpful while setting a process instead of a hard no.
psychology: Autonomy and clarity calm people more than rigid policy talk.
application: Offer a path and timeline before quoting restrictions.

speaker: Customer

options.text: Have you tried turning it off and on?
Sorry about that. Which device and when did it last crash?

why: Empathy plus diagnostic detail gets you to a real fix faster.
psychology: Being believed matters as much as the technical answer.
application: Collect device, timing, and steps before suggesting fixes.

speaker: Customer
prompt: I already explained this to three people.

options.text: I have your notes here. Let me summarize what I see, then we’ll finish this.

why: Showing continuity proves respect for their time and prior effort.
psychology: Repeated storytelling fuels resentment; recognition reduces it.
application: Recap known facts before asking anything new.

speaker: Customer
prompt: Can you just make an exception?

options.text: I can’t break policy, but I can find the closest option that still helps.

why: Boundaries stay firm while creativity keeps goodwill intact.
psychology: People accept no better when paired with a real alternative.
application: Refuse the ask, offer the next-best workable path.

speaker: Customer

options.text: I’d hate to lose you. What’s the main thing we haven’t solved yet?

why: Curiosity turns an exit threat into actionable feedback.
psychology: Exit talk often masks one unmet need worth solving.
application: Ask for the decisive issue before accepting churn.

speaker: Customer

options.text: You’re right to expect updates. I’ll own the next checkpoint and time.

why: Ownership and a concrete next step repair reliability.
psychology: Accountability restores trust faster than explanations.
application: State who will do what by when.

speaker: Customer

options.text: Let’s review the invoice line by line together.

why: Joint review signals transparency and invites shared discovery.
psychology: Suspicion drops when the process becomes visible.
application: Walk through charges with the customer, not at them.

speaker: Customer

options.text: I’ll prioritize it. Here’s what I can commit to before end of day.

why: Urgency is met with a specific, honest commitment.
psychology: Clear expectations beat vague reassurance.
application: State the deliverable and the clock, then deliver.

speaker: Customer
prompt: Why should I stay with you?

options.text: Based on your goals, here’s the value we uniquely deliver—and a plan to improve.

why: Value is tied to their goals plus a recovery plan.
psychology: Self-interest beats brand slogans in retention talks.
application: Mirror their outcomes, then show the next win.

speaker: Customer

options.text: I’m a real person here. Tell me what felt off so I can help better.
That’s just how the system works.

why: Human presence plus invitation to feedback re-humanizes the channel.
psychology: People soften when they feel treated as individuals.
application: Signal humanity, then ask what would feel more helpful.

speaker: Customer

options.text: I can escalate. First I’ll capture the issue so the next person has full context.
You’ll wait longer if you escalate.

why: You honor the request while improving handoff quality.
psychology: Feeling stuck drives escalation; competence restores confidence.
application: Agree to escalate and package a clean summary.

speaker: Customer
prompt: I don’t trust your company anymore.

options.text: Trust takes time to rebuild. What would a trustworthy next step look like to you?

why: You accept the breach and co-define repair.
psychology: Trust returns through consistent small proofs, not claims.
application: Ask them to define the proof they need next.

speaker: Customer

options.text: Which part feels unclear? I’ll walk you through the fastest path.

why: You localize the friction and offer guided help.
psychology: Confusion is vulnerability; guidance restores competence.
application: Ask where they got stuck, then demo the short path.

speaker: Customer
prompt: I’m not happy with the outcome.

options.text: Understood. What outcome were you hoping for?

why: You explore the gap between expectation and result.
psychology: Unspoken expectations fuel disappointment.
application: Clarify the desired end state before defending process.

speaker: Customer

options.text: Of course we care—our NPS is high.
Yes. Caring looks like fixing this with you. What’s the priority?

why: Care is shown through action, not slogans.
psychology: Abstract claims fail; concrete help proves intent.
application: Translate empathy into a prioritized next action.

speaker: Customer

options.text: Let’s compare what was promised with what you have, then close the gap.

why: You treat the promise as data and aim to reconcile it.
psychology: Broken expectations demand repair, not deflection.
application: Align promise vs delivery, then propose a make-good.

speaker: Customer
prompt: Can you speak to a manager?

options.text: I am empowered to resolve this. If we still need a manager after that, I’ll connect you.

why: You assert capability while keeping escalation available.
psychology: People escalate when they feel powerless with the current agent.
application: Show authority first; escalate if still unresolved.

speaker: Prospect
prompt: Who is this and why are you calling?

options.text: Quick intro: I’m [Name] from [Company]. We help teams cut onboarding time—got 30 seconds?

why: Identity, relevance, and a short ask respect their time.
psychology: Uncertainty spikes hang-ups; clarity earns a beat.
application: Name, company, benefit, and a micro-permission.

speaker: Prospect
prompt: We’re happy with our current vendor.

options.text: Glad that’s working. If priorities shift, what would make a second look worthwhile?

why: You respect status quo while planting a future trigger.
psychology: Attacking loyalty hardens resistance.
application: Acknowledge satisfaction, then ask for the switch criteria.

speaker: Prospect

options.text: Sure—what should the email focus on so it’s useful, not noise?

why: You accept the channel and sharpen relevance.
psychology: Brush-offs soften when the next touch feels customized.
application: Confirm topic and success criteria before sending.

speaker: Prospect

options.text: Totally fair. When’s a better two-minute window this week?

why: You honor timing and book a concrete alternative.
psychology: Respect for attention builds reciprocity.
application: Offer a short reschedule with a specific window.

speaker: Prospect
prompt: How did you get my number?

options.text: From a public business listing. Happy to explain why I reached out.

why: Transparency reduces creepiness and recenters purpose.
psychology: Source opacity triggers distrust.
application: State the source plainly, then the reason for contact.

speaker: Client
prompt: We need 30% off or we walk.

options.text: If we adjust price, what scope or term can we adjust with it?

why: You trade value instead of conceding unilaterally.
psychology: Anchors lose power when you introduce variables.
application: Link discounts to term, volume, or scope changes.

speaker: Client

options.text: Price is one factor. Which outcomes matter most beyond sticker cost?

why: You reframe from price to total value criteria.
psychology: Comparison shoppers still care about risk and results.
application: Ask which success metrics outweigh unit price.

speaker: Client

options.text: Unlimited isn’t workable. We can include two revision rounds and a change-order path after.

why: You protect scope while offering a structured process.
psychology: Infinite options create anxiety; structure creates safety.
application: Cap revisions and define the exception path.

speaker: Client
prompt: Can you start before we sign?

options.text: I can share a prep checklist now; work begins after signature to protect both sides.

why: You keep momentum without skipping commitment.
psychology: Helpfulness without boundaries invites scope creep.
application: Offer low-risk prep; require agreement for delivery.

speaker: Client

options.text: Understood. If that’s final, here’s what we can deliver at that number.

why: You treat the number as real and resize the package accordingly.
psychology: Matching offer to scope avoids deadlocks.
application: Accept the constraint, then adjust deliverables.

speaker: Teammate
prompt: I missed the deadline. Everything piled up.

options.text: Let’s separate what blocked you from what’s still recoverable today.

why: You diagnose blockers and triage remaining work.
psychology: Shame freezes performance; clarity restores agency.
application: Review causes, then replan the critical path.

speaker: Teammate
why: Dissent becomes useful information instead of conflict.
psychology: Curiosity converts status battles into problem-solving.
application: Invite the strongest counterargument before deciding.

speaker: Teammate

options.text: Thanks for saying it. What’s one load we can cut this week?

why: You validate and take a concrete relief action.
psychology: Burnout needs resource change, not pep talks.
application: Remove or postpone one real demand immediately.

speaker: Teammate

options.text: I do. I’ll decide by 3pm after one more input from design.

why: Clear ownership and a deadline kill ambiguity.
psychology: Diffusion of responsibility stalls teams.
application: Name the owner, input needed, and decide-by time.

speaker: Teammate
prompt: The other team keeps blocking us.

options.text: Let’s map the dependency and I’ll escalate with a proposed unblock.

why: You convert frustration into a structured escalation.
psychology: Venting without a path deepens helplessness.
application: Document the block and propose the unblock request.

speaker: New contact

options.text: I help product teams ship clearer customer messaging—curious what you’re working on?

why: A crisp value line plus a question makes it a conversation.
psychology: People engage when you show interest after context.
application: One-sentence role, then ask about them.

speaker: New contact

options.text: I’d like that. What’s the best way to follow up this week?

why: You convert politeness into a specific next step.
psychology: Vague intent dies without logistics.
application: Agree, then choose channel and timing.

speaker: New contact
prompt: I don’t really need anything right now.

options.text: No ask today—happy to share a resource if useful later. Mind if I connect on LinkedIn?

why: Low-pressure follow-up preserves goodwill.
psychology: People remember generosity more than pitches.
application: Offer optional value; request a light connection.

speaker: Colleague
prompt: You threw me under the bus in that meeting.

options.text: I hear that landed badly. What specifically felt unfair?

why: You acknowledge impact and invite specifics.
psychology: Defensiveness escalates; curiosity de-escalates.
application: Validate impact first, then examine facts together.

speaker: Colleague
prompt: We keep talking past each other.

options.text: Let’s each restate the other’s point before we respond.
I’m being clear; you’re not listening.

why: Reflective listening forces shared understanding.
psychology: Mishearing often looks like disagreement.
application: Use paraphrase rounds before debating.

speaker: Colleague

options.text: That’s serious. What would need to change for us to work together again?

why: You treat the rupture as negotiable conditions.
psychology: Absolute statements often hide repairable needs.
application: Ask for change conditions before accepting a split.

speaker: Buyer

options.text: Happy to. So I send the right tier—what size team and main use case?

why: You qualify before dumping numbers.
psychology: Unanchored pricing invites the lowest tier comparison.
application: Ask fit questions, then share relevant pricing.

speaker: Buyer

options.text: Makes sense. What criteria will decide the winner?

why: You uncover the decision scorecard.
psychology: Vague evaluation hides missing champions or criteria.
application: Ask how they’ll choose, by when, and with whom.

speaker: Buyer

options.text: Got it. What happens if that feature is missing in month one?

why: You test whether it’s true must-have vs nice-to-have.
psychology: Stated requirements often inflate under pressure.
application: Probe consequence to prioritize real blockers.

speaker: Audience member
prompt: Can you get to the point?

options.text: Absolutely—the one takeaway is X. Here’s the 20-second version.

why: You honor the ask with a crisp headline.
psychology: Attention recovers when value becomes immediate.
application: Lead with the takeaway, then optional detail.

speaker: Audience member

options.text: Fair challenge. Here’s the evidence, and here’s where I could be wrong.

why: Confidence plus intellectual humility builds credibility.
psychology: Certainty without caveats sounds fragile.
application: Share evidence and your falsification conditions.

speaker: Client
prompt: Just tell us what to do.

options.text: I will. First I need the constraint that matters most: speed, cost, or risk?

why: Recommendations need a priority frame to be useful.
psychology: Advice without constraints feels generic.
application: Clarify the tradeoff, then recommend.

speaker: Client

options.text: Helpful—what made it fail last time, so we don’t repeat it?

why: Past failure becomes diagnostic input.
psychology: People resist recycled advice that ignored history.
application: Ask what was tried, measured, and blocked.

speaker: Date
prompt: I had a weird day. Maybe I’m bad company tonight.

options.text: Thanks for saying that. Want to vent a bit, or prefer a lighter topic?

why: You offer choice and emotional safety.
psychology: Autonomy in conversation lowers social pressure.
application: Acknowledge, then let them set the depth.

speaker: Date
prompt: I’m not sure this is a match.

options.text: I appreciate the honesty. What felt off, if you’re open to sharing?

why: Graceful curiosity keeps dignity on both sides.
psychology: Defensiveness confirms the mismatch.
application: Thank them, invite optional feedback, accept the answer.
